title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook - Onboarding, Escalation, Integration, QBRs (Comprehensive)
author: Ava Patel
summary:
Purpose: This single, comprehensive playbook describes Redwood Inference's standard approach for enterprise customer onboarding, integration handoffs, operational support, escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, and recurring health checks / QBR materials. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Support, Solutions Engineering (SE), and on-call Engineering partners.

Scope: Covers pre-sales handoff and first 90 days of onboarding, ongoing support processes, severity definitions and technical escalation matrix, integration checklist for API and private deployments, an itemized list of frequent issues and mitigations, and templates for monthly health checks and quarterly business reviews (QBRs).
audience: Customer Success Managers, Solutions Engineers, Support Engineers, Account Executives, SRE/Platform engineers, Customer technical contacts
prerequisites: Customer has signed MSA or order form; contact list and AEs/CSM SE assigned; access to customer's onboarding Slack/Zoom and required network info; if Private deployment: access to customer's VPC/VPN and KMS instructions
roles_and_ownership:
Roles and responsibilities
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): primary relationship owner, coordinates onboarding milestones, schedules QBRs.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): technical integration lead during onboarding; runs POC and test prompts; validates performance targets.
- Support Engineer (Tier 1/2): triages incoming tickets, performs diagnostics, owns known-issue workarounds.
- SRE / Runtime Engineering: owns platform incidents, capacity, and escalations for severity >=2.
- Account Executive (AE): commercial touchpoints and contract/renewal coordination.

Ownership table (text representation)
| Area | Primary owner | Backup |
| Onboarding project management | CSM | AE |
| API/SDK integration | SE | Support Engineer |
| Dedicated / Private deployment setup | SE & eng-private-deployments | eng-infra |
| Incident response and escalations | Support Engineer | SRE |
| QBR and adoption metrics | CSM | Customer Success Ops |
pre_onboarding_checklist:
Pre-Onboarding checklist (to be completed before kick-off)
1) Contract & SOW signed, billing contact confirmed.
2) Customer tech contact list (emails/phone/Slack) provided.
3) Use-case and expected QPS/p99 latency targets documented.
4) Data residency and compliance requirements (e.g., EU data residency) specified.
5) Environment type declared: Hosted / Dedicated / Private.
6) For Private: network/egress requirements, firewall whitelist, KMS/HSM details, onprem packaging constraints.
7) Provisioning info: desired model(s), token quota, rate limits, initial feature flags (streaming, function-calls).
8) Kick-off meeting scheduled with CSM, SE, customer engineering stakeholders.
30_60_90_day_onboarding_plan:
Suggested 30/60/90 day milestones
- Day 0: Kickoff - review goals, success metrics, schedule weekly cadences.
- Week 1 (0-7 days): Access and credentials (API keys, org-level settings), basic smoke tests, sample prompt tests, billing setup confirmed.
- Week 2-3 (8-21 days): Integration: SDK/REST integration, authentication, rate limiting behavior validated, basic observability (per-route latency/cost) dashboard created.
- Week 4-6 (22-45 days): Performance tuning: batching, caching, quantization suggestions from Redwood Optimize; run load test at target QPS; validate p50/p95/p99; finalize model pinning and rollout policy.
- Week 7-12 (46-90 days): Production readiness: failover and fallback policies validated, on-call contacts added, playbooks handed to customer ops, first health check and QBR scheduling, adoption plan for next quarter.
- Deliverables by day 90: Shared dashboard, runbook & escalation contact card, agreed SLO targets, first QBR slide deck template with baseline metrics.
integration_guide:
Integration checklist & examples
1) Authentication and API keys
   - Hosted: Issue API key scoped to project/org. Keys should be rotated per company policy.
   - Dedicated/Private: mutual TLS or pre-shared token; follow SE instruction doc.
2) Network & IP allowlist
   - Provide Redwood egress IP ranges if required for hosted integrations. For Private, verify VPN/BGP configuration.
3) Sample REST smoke test (curl)
   - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' -d '{"model":"rwd-ggml-13b","input":"Hello"}'
4) Webhooks and callbacks
   - Configure callback endpoint with TLS 1.2+, provide public endpoint or configure internal routing for Private.
5) Rate limits and quotas
   - Default hosted rate limits provided in contract; SE to coordinate increases during load tests.
6) Observability hooks
   - Send request IDs for tracing (x-request-id). Activate per-route dashboards and link to Redwood Console.
7) Private deployment specifics
   - KMS integration: provide key ARN and roles.
   - Image/Package deployment: follow onprem-packaging checklist for host requirements (GPU type, driver versions, CUDA/ROCm).
8) Acceptance tests (examples)
   - Functional: end-to-end response with sample prompts.
   - Performance: 10 minute sustained run at target QPS with latency reporting.
   - Security: authenticated access only, audit log verification.
escalation_playbook:
Severity definitions and escalation matrix
- Severity 1 (S1) - Critical outage: Platform unavailable for customer production traffic for >5 minutes, data loss, or security incident.
  - Initial action: Immediate paging to SRE and Support Lead.
  - Contacts: SRE on-call -> Support Lead -> CSM -> VP Eng if unresolved at 30 minutes.
  - Communication: Post on incident channel, update customer every 15 minutes until mitigation.
- Severity 2 (S2) - Major degradation: Significant increase in latency/failed requests impacting majority of users.
  - Initial action: Support triage, replicate, involve runtime engineers.
  - Contacts: Support -> Runtime Engineering -> SE.
  - Communication: Update customer every 60 minutes.
- Severity 3 (S3) - Partial impact: Single-route regression, elevated error rates for a small subset.
  - Action: Standard ticket, worked during business hours by Support and SE.
- Severity 4 (S4) - Informational/feature request.

Escalation matrix (text):
- Support T1: triage and collect diagnostics (request IDs, timestamps, route, model, region, sample prompt).
- Support T2: reproduce, apply temporary mitigation (circuit breaker, route rewrite), escalate to Runtime Eng if root cause involves infra or model serving.
- Runtime Eng: owns fixes for kernel/runtime issues, communicates ETA.
- SE / Private Deployments team: handles network/packaging/KMS escalations with customer infra teams.

Ticket closure and RCA policy
1) For S1/S2 incidents with customer impact, produce interim incident updates and a written RCA within 72 hours.
2) Full RCA and remediation plan published to customer and internal incident channel within 7 business days.
support_process_and_workflow:
Support intake & SLA
- Intake channels: Support portal ticket, email, in-product 'Help' widget, customer Slack workspace (if provisioned).
- Triage steps: Acknowledge within 1 business hour (target), classify severity, assign owner.
- SLAs (internal targets):
  - Initial response: S1 15 min (paging); S2 60 min; S3 4 hours; S4 2 business days.
  - Resolution: Dependent on cause; provide ETA to customer within first update.
- Diagnostic checklist for Support Engineers:
  1) Verify request IDs and timestamps; pull logs and per-route metrics.
  2) Reproduce error with same prompt/headers.
  3) Check model variant, quantization profile, and region routing.
  4) Confirm quota/rate-limit exceeded or authentication failures.
  5) Apply documented workarounds from known_issues list if applicable.
- Communication: Use templated updates for consistency (status, scope, mitigation, ETA).
known_issues_and_workarounds:
Known issues (common patterns)
1) High p99 latency on long-context prompts
   - Symptoms: p99 spikes when prompts include >8k tokens.
   - Root causes: model architecture + KV cache pressure + suboptimal batching.
   - Workarounds: enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts; suggest shorter system prompts; use recommended quantization profile and increase batch timeout slightly; consider model variant with better long-context performance.
2) Intermittent 'KV cache miss' errors on dedicated pools after scale events
   - Symptoms: errors immediately following autoscale up/down.
   - Workarounds: implement client retries with exponential backoff (recommended: 3 retries with jitter), and enable session stickiness during scheduled scale events.
3) Authentication failures after key rotation
   - Symptoms: 401s for a subset of requests after rolling key rotation.
   - Workarounds: advise customers to stagger key rotation, update SDKs to support 429 backoff and graceful retries; ensure clock skew <5s if using signed tokens.
4) Embedding drift / quality regressions after model rollout
   - Symptoms: embeddings similarity metrics drop in evaluation set.
   - Workarounds: rollback to previous model variant, run Redwood Optimize suggestion report, run synthetic evals and small-scale A/B test before wider rollout.
5) Webhook delivery failures due to TLS negotiation
   - Symptoms: 504s or handshake failures logged.
   - Workarounds: validate server supports TLS1.2+, confirm cipher suites, provide self-signed cert procedure for Private deployments.
qbr_and_health_check_materials:
Health checks and QBR templates
1) Recurring health check (monthly) checklist
   - Verify API key usage & quota consumption.
   - Review per-route cost and latency (p50/p95/p99) and surface anomalies.
   - Error rate review (5xx, auth, timeouts) and recent incidents.
   - Adoption metrics: active users, calls/day, embeddings per day, burst patterns.
   - Action items and owner for each anomaly.
2) Quarterly Business Review (QBR) template
   - Slide 1: Executive summary (uptime, availability, adoption highlights).
   - Slide 2: Production metrics vs targets (SLO attainment, latency & cost trends).
   - Slide 3: Usage breakdown (models, routes, regions).
   - Slide 4: Incidents & reliability improvements (RCAs & mitigations since last QBR).
   - Slide 5: Optimization opportunities (batching, quantization, model variants) and projected cost savings.
   - Slide 6: Roadmap & feature requests, next steps and success metrics for next quarter.
3) Health dashboard links and KPIs to track
   - KPIs: availability (goal 99.95%), p95 latency target by route, cost per 1k tokens, error rate <0.5% for production routes.
   - Dashboards: per-account route latency/cost, embeddings usage, model-variant rollouts, audit logs.
templates_and_snippets:
Useful templates (copyable)
- Incident update template: [Time] [Severity] [Scope] [Mitigation] [Next ETA] [Owner].
- QBR agenda template: 1) Exec summary 2) Metrics 3) Incidents & followups 4) Optimization opportunities 5) Roadmap 6) Action items.
- Post-onboarding handoff checklist: Shared dashboard link, runbook link, support contact card, escalation contact list, SLOs & acceptance test evidence.
